response: Yes, acute changes in heart rate induced by isoproterenol can affect aortic stiffness in patients with hypertension. Isoproterenol, a beta-adrenergic agonist, increases heart rate and can lead to changes in aortic stiffness. Studies have shown that increased heart rate can decrease aortic stiffness, possibly due to the increased contractility of the heart and subsequent changes in blood pressure and vascular properties. However, the exact mechanisms and clinical implications of this effect in patients with hypertension require further investigation.
